summary: Tip: review of records access and transfers on 2026-11-10. Evidence supports an incident sequence on the nurse workstation (ws-nurse-01, 10.20.1.21) under account tmori, console session workstation#72. (1) At 09:56:38Z a clinic-export of the patients_full dataset wrote /home/tmori/Downloads/rx-7f3.db; records app logged a 16.6 MB export_bulk for tmori, corroborated by the collector copy, the tap, and fs_stat (ev_244bd0403704, ev_cf00835d7acf, ev_52d40eda9460, ev_d080620c9c7b, ev_e99c55f7d89b). (2) At 09:59:41Z the file was uploaded with curl to 10.20.9.15:8080, 16.65 MB out on the tap. That is over the 5 MB threshold and not an approved destination (ev_6912341a9ccd, ev_96abab423307). (3) A session-72 login at 09:55:47Z is present in the collector copy but missing from the workstation's local auth.log, which is consistent with local log removal; rotation does not explain it (ev_7d20d518a543, ev_39e6469fed9d, ev_391d2a3b9525). Confidence 0.75, since a write fault is not excluded. (4) The records access.log gap from 06:18 to 08:52 is explained by scheduled rotation with off-host archive and is not an incident. Attribution: account tmori was used; human operator not established. Shared credentials and remote VPN use are not excluded, and no person is named.

What is 10.20.9.15:8080, and was rx-7f3.db received there? The tap shows bytes only, not content.
Is the missing auth.log line deliberate deletion or a local write fault? Check the workstation's filesystem and the .1 rotated generation.
